title: Compress the Easy, Explore the Hard: Difficulty-Aware Entropy Regularization for Efficient LLM Reasoning

problem.claim: Verbose explicit reasoning steps increase inference latency and computational costs, limiting real-world LLM deployment.

gap.claim: Existing compression approaches can sacrifice reasoning capability for brevity, and shorter-trajectory optimization can cause entropy collapse that limits exploration on difficult questions.

contributions.claim: CEEH is a difficulty-aware reinforcement-learning approach that selectively compresses reasoning for easy questions and preserves exploration for hard questions.
CEEH uses selective entropy regularization to preserve a diverse search space for hard questions while enabling stronger compression on easier instances.
CEEH introduces a dynamic optimal-length penalty anchored to the historically shortest correct response.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Across six reasoning benchmarks, CEEH reportedly reduces response length while maintaining accuracy comparable to the base model.
CEEH reportedly improves Pass@k relative to length-only optimization.
The dynamic optimal-length penalty reportedly counteracts entropy-induced length inflation and stabilizes the reward signal.

narrative_sequence.summary: Explicit reasoning improves complex-task performance but creates deployment costs through verbosity.
Existing compression methods may trade reasoning capability for shorter responses.
Shorter-trajectory optimization can collapse entropy and restrict valid-path exploration, especially on difficult questions.
CEEH applies difficulty-aware entropy regularization and a dynamic length penalty.
The authors report shorter responses, comparable accuracy, and improved Pass@k across six benchmarks.

source_observation.claim: Shorter reasoning trajectories may reduce exploration for difficult questions through entropy collapse.

interpretation.claim: Efficiency objectives may need to vary with instance difficulty rather than impose a uniform brevity target.

application.claim: For adaptive reasoning systems, preserve search diversity on hard instances and compress established reasoning paths on easy instances.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported reasoning benchmarks or model setting.

unknowns: The six benchmark identities are unspecified.
The base model, training configuration, and comparison methods are unspecified.
The abstract does not provide quantitative response-length, accuracy, or Pass@k results.
Independent verification and reproducibility details are unavailable.
